step1_analysis.circuit_type: LVDS Receiver / Differential to Single-Ended Amplifier
step1_analysis.description: A high-speed LVDS receiver front-end consisting of a PMOS differential pair with a symmetric cross-coupled NMOS active load, followed by a push-pull output stage. It converts a low-swing differential input signal into a full-swing single-ended output.

paper_reference.title: LVDS I/O Interface for Gb/s-per-Pin Operation in 0.35-m CMOS

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the receiver circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a 200uA tail current (added for proper biasing). The second stage mirrors the active load current (~100uA per branch). Total current ~400uA. Power = 400uA * 1.8V = 0.72mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down from 0.35um 3.3V to 130nm 1.8V. The 33mW in the paper likely includes the transmitter and full I/O pad ring, whereas this is just the receiver front-end.

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency differential to single-ended voltage gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: The cross-coupled active load provides high impedance ~ 1/(gm_diode - gm_cross). With equal sizing, gain is very high, limited by channel length modulation. The push-pull second stage adds more gain.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cross-coupled load significantly boosts the DC gain compared to a standard diode-connected load, acting almost like a latch.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the output pole and internal node capacitances. With L=0.5um, parasitic caps are moderate.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 is faster than 0.35um, but the L=0.5um sizing limits the maximum bandwidth compared to using minimum length (0.15um) devices.

propagation_delay.description: Time delay from the input differential zero-crossing to the output reaching VDD/2.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay is roughly C_load * VDD / I_out. With 50fF load and ~100uA drive, delay ~ 50fF * 0.9V / 100uA = 450ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the load capacitance and the tail current bias.

input_sensitivity.description: Minimum differential input voltage required to switch the output.

sky130_expected.calculation: The high gain of the cross-coupled stage ensures sharp switching. Offset voltage (not simulated here) would dominate in reality.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal simulation will show very high sensitivity (<1mV), but practical sensitivity is limited by mismatch and hysteresis.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for LVDS receiver measuring power, AC gain, bandwidth, transient delay, and DC switching threshold.
step3_testbench.spice:
* LVDS Receiver Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u

XM1 N0 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N3 N3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 LABEL_NET_0 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N4 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N3 LABEL_NET_1 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N3 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N1 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N1 N3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM9 N0 N3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM10 N4 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}

* Power supply and missing tail current source
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
I_tail VDD N2 200u

* Input signals (Common mode = 1.25V as per paper, AC diff = 1V, Transient diff = 350mVpp)
VCM VCM 0 1.25
VDIFF VDIFF 0 dc 0 ac 1 pulse(-0.175 0.175 0 100p 100p 400p 1n)
B_IN_P LABEL_NET_0 0 V=v(VCM) + v(VDIFF)/2
B_IN_N LABEL_NET_1 0 V=v(VCM) - v(VDIFF)/2

* Load capacitance
C_load N4 0 50f

.control
  * DC Operating Point
  op
  let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print power

  * AC Analysis
  ac dec 50 1Meg 10G
  let gain_db = vdb(N4)
  meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1Meg
  let gain_3db = dc_gain - 3
  meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1

  * Transient Analysis
  tran 10p 5n
  meas tran v_out_max max v(N4)
  meas tran v_out_min min v(N4)
  meas tran delay_rise trig v(VDIFF) val=0 rise=2 targ v(N4) val=0.9 rise=2
  meas tran delay_fall trig v(VDIFF) val=0 fall=2 targ v(N4) val=0.9 fall=2

  * DC Sweep for Transfer Characteristic
  dc VDIFF -0.5 0.5 0.01
  meas dc vth_switch when v(N4)=0.9 rise=1
  
  quit
.endc
.end
